'''Weyl's tube formula''' gives the [[volume]] of an object defined as the set of all points within a small distance of a [[manifold]].

Let <math>\Sigma</math> be an [[orientability|oriented]], closed, two-dimensional surface, and let <math>N_\varepsilon(\Sigma)</math> denote the set of all points within a distance <math>\varepsilon</math> of the surface <math>\Sigma</math>. Then, for <math>\varepsilon</math> sufficiently small, the volume of <math>N_\varepsilon(\Sigma)</math> is
:<math>V = 2A(\Sigma)\varepsilon + \frac{4\pi}{3} \chi(\Sigma)\varepsilon^3,</math>
where <math>A(\Sigma)</math> is the [[area]] of the surface and <math>\chi(\Sigma)</math> is its [[Euler characteristic]]. This expression can be generalized to the case where <math>\Sigma</math> is a <math>q</math>-dimensional [[submanifold]] of <math>n</math>-dimensional [[Euclidean space]] <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>.
